name: Ahobilam Nava Narasimha — the Nine Shrines of the Man-Lion
theme: Nine shrines of Narasimha scattered through the forested Nallamala hills, where tradition places the god's appearance to save Prahlada
description: Ahobilam, in the Nallamala hills, is revered as the place where Vishnu emerged as Narasimha, the man-lion, to destroy Hiranyakashipu and protect the boy Prahlada. Around the main temple of Upper Ahobilam, nine shrines honour nine aspects of Narasimha: fierce at Jwala, where the battle is said to have reached its climax, gentle with Lakshmi at Malola, boar-faced at Varaha, and teaching yoga to Prahlada at Yogananda, among others. Some lie beside the road between Lower and Upper Ahobilam; others are reached only by forest trails, streams and rock steps, and pilgrims often hire a local guide. Ahobilam is also a Divya Desam sung by Thirumangai Alvar and the seat of the Ahobila Matha.
